newsitem.title: UK: NWE high sulphur fuel oil eases again.
newsitem.headline: NWE high sulphur fuel oil eases again.

text.p: NWE high sulphur cracked fuel oil eased again on Monday because of good supply and limited end user demand, traders said.
High sulphur barges were traded at $91, $92 and $92.50 fob ARA. Prices then rose to be talked around $92/$94. Bunker demand was poor.
High sulphur cargoes were heard offered at $97 a tonne cif NWE by a trader. The same trader was heard to have sold a cargo on Friday to a utility at $97 cif NWE.
A refiner in northern France was heard to have sold a high density cargo to the same trader on Friday at a $5 discount to the mean of published fob quotes.
Low sulphur cargoes were weaker too, amid healthy supply at the end of the month. Italian buying was not thought likely to kick in until the last week of February or March, at the earliest.
Traders said Turkey's Tupras had tendered to buy one 50,000 tonne cargo of low sulphur fuel oil, for delivery between February 20-25. The tender closes on Thursday.
